threat_event: Ransomware on the shared laptop encrypts the synced cloud drive (contracts, code spreadsheet, report exports, video) and the attacker copies files first
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Laptop shared with a family member under one account; no backup outside the sync service; email on text-message MFA; no security training
affected_asset_or_process: SYS-04 laptop; SYS-02 email and files; BP-02 alarm response
regulatory_driver: Fla. Stat. 501.171(2); Fla. Stat. 501.171(4); Fla. Stat. 493.6121(2); client agreements (24-hour notice)
existing_controls: Full-disk encryption; built-in antivirus; automatic updates
treatment_plan: Separate family and business accounts on the laptop; versioned backup the laptop cannot overwrite; codes out of the spreadsheet; annual training; P08 runbook

threat_event: Takeover of the patrol app admin account exposes every client's post orders, codes, and incident reports, and lets the attacker alter or delete reports
threat_source: Cybercriminal (credential stuffing with a breached password)
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Admin password reused and found in a public breach list; no MFA on the admin account
treatment_plan: Turn on app-based MFA for the admin account with recovery codes in the home safe; password manager; monthly sign-in review

threat_event: Client alarm codes, gate codes, or keyholder lists are exposed and used to enter a client site (burglary or theft at the client's property)
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Codes in an unprotected spreadsheet, a phone note, client text threads shown on the lock screen, and patrol app post orders; former client's codes never removed; no rule to ask clients to change codes
affected_asset_or_process: Client sites; BP-02; client access data
treatment_plan: Move codes into the password manager vault with one sealed paper copy in the home safe; delete the spreadsheet, note, and old texts; hide previews; ask clients to stop texting codes and to change codes after any suspected exposure

threat_event: Client keys or access cards are lost or stolen from the patrol vehicle, and the site-name labels show which property they open
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: All 23 keys on one ring labeled with site names; no vehicle lockbox; no periodic key inventory
regulatory_driver: Fla. Stat. 493.6118(1)(e); client agreements (2-hour notice; return of keys)
existing_controls: Paper key log; vehicle locked when parked
treatment_plan: Coded tags in place of site names, with the code key in the password manager; bolted vehicle lockbox; monthly key count against the log

threat_event: The phone is lost or stolen, exposing texted codes, the logged-in patrol app, and MFA codes
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 4-digit passcode; message previews on the lock screen; codes in a note; remote erase never tested
existing_controls: Device encryption; remote locate and erase turned on
treatment_plan: Longer passcode; hide previews; codes only in the password manager; test remote erase once a year; spare phone ready at home

threat_event: Body-camera video of people (faces, injuries, conversations) is disclosed through public links or a lost storage card, or audio is recorded without the consent Florida law requires
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Video kept indefinitely; unencrypted card; 14 public links with no expiry; recording not always announced
treatment_plan: Expire all public links; share clips only by expiring links to named people; 90-day retention unless tied to an incident; announce recording at the start of every contact; counsel confirms when audio may be recorded

threat_event: The owner is hurt on patrol, ill, or without the phone, so nobody patrols, answers alarms, or can open client sites
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: One person holds every role, key, code, and credential; backup agency arrangement is verbal and holds nothing
regulatory_driver: Client agreements (45-minute alarm response; nightly patrols)
existing_controls: Verbal arrangement with a licensed backup agency (license confirmed 2026-08-11)
treatment_plan: Written coverage agreement with confidentiality terms; sealed code book and emergency sheet in the home safe; second contact given to alarm companies (P05)

threat_event: The AI report assistant labels an urgent event as routine, so the client is not alerted, or it puts wrong details into a report the owner then sends
threat_source: AI tool error (patrol app AI report assistant)
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Priority label decided which events alert clients; no rule to review each draft line by line; near miss on 2026-07-19 (water leak labeled routine)
treatment_plan: Owner sets the priority on every report; phone call to the client for any fire, water, intrusion, injury, or police event; read every draft in full before submitting (P10)

threat_event: Former client staff keep reading incident reports and post orders through the client portal
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Client portal accounts never reviewed; 3 of 12 stale; no MFA for client users
existing_controls: Each account sees only its own site
treatment_plan: Remove the 3 stale accounts; quarterly review; ask each client to report departures; require MFA for client users

threat_event: Takeover of the email account is used to send clients fake invoices with new bank details
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Email on text-message MFA; clients pay by ACH link and have never been told how bank changes are announced
existing_controls: Text-message MFA; accounting SaaS payment links
treatment_plan: Authenticator app MFA on email; tell every client in writing that bank details never change by email; sign-in alerts on

threat_event: A security incident is not recognized, or a client or breach notice deadline is missed
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No incident plan, contact list, or knowledge of the 30-day Florida clock and the 2-hour client clause
regulatory_driver: Fla. Stat. 501.171(3); Fla. Stat. 501.171(4); client agreements (2-hour and 24-hour notice)
treatment_plan: Adopt the P08 runbook and printed contact list; walk it through with the IT technician; annual training

threat_event: Records cannot be produced to the Department on request, or are kept far longer than needed
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No retention schedule; records spread across SaaS services; ransomware could make them unavailable
existing_controls: Patrol app keeps reports; paper key log
treatment_plan: Retention schedule in POL-01 8.8; yearly export of 2 years of reports to the backup; counsel confirms that cloud storage meets 'maintained in this state'

threat_event: The owner receives criminal justice information (for example a warrant list or a criminal history result) from a law enforcement contact and stores it in the patrol app or email
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No rule against accepting it; the owner talks with deputies on most shifts
regulatory_driver: C-EMERGENCY-R01 (CJIS Security Policy; no access agreement); C-EMERGENCY-R02 (28 CFR 20.21(f))
treatment_plan: POL-01 9.6: never accept or store criminal justice information; delete and tell the sender if received

threat_event: A hurricane stops patrols for several days and damages the home office
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: One vehicle; home office in a storm area
existing_controls: Patrol app and SaaS are cloud-hosted; clients suspend patrols by contract during declared storm emergencies
treatment_plan: Accepted: residual risk Low. Take the laptop, keys, and code book in a sealed bag when evacuating

threat_event: The patrol app is unavailable during a shift, so scans and reports are not recorded
regulatory_driver: Client agreements (nightly patrols; reports by 6:30 a.m.)
existing_controls: Offline mode on the phone; vendor RTO 8 hours (SOC 2, P09)
treatment_plan: Accepted: residual risk Low. Paper patrol log and time-stamped photos if the app fails
